title: Iconic NASA space telescope has burned up in Earth's atmosphere
excerpt: Following a failed attempt to save the stricken observatory, the telescope plummeted to Earth after 22 years of operations.
content:
Space & Astronomy

By T.K. Randall
November 5, 2026


Image: AI-generated (Midjourney)

Following a failed attempt to save the stricken observatory, the telescope plummeted to Earth after 22 years of operations.

Launched back on November 20th, 2004, the Swift Space Telescope, which was designed to study gamma-ray bursts, had originally been intended to operate for only two years.

Nonetheless, it ended up providing valuable data for more than two decades.

Sadly, though, its orbit had been steadily decaying during this time, and when a planned rescue mission designed to extend its life ultimately fell through, the observatory's fate was sealed.

Now, according to NASA, the orbital telescope entered Earth's atmosphere on November 4th and burned up somewhere above the North Sumatra region of Indonesia.

While it's possible that some of its components survived and made it to the ground, the vast majority has been utterly destroyed, marking a sad end to this iconic window on the cosmos.

Source: NASA.gov
